title: Harden CI child-process cleanup
description: Follow-up from the TASK-1.19 and TASK-1.20 reviews. In rare cases a hung or unkillable child process can outlive its test or attempt, wasting up to the 13-minute step backstop or leaving orphans on a runner.

nodes.title: Bootstrap the strict TypeScript project with one-command checks
Run every check in GitHub Actions on each push and pull request
Retry the stalled Playwright system-dependency install in CI
Keep strict wall-clock speed checks out of the CI test run

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given tools/ci/retry.js times out an attempt and both SIGTERM and SIGKILL to the process group fail with EPERM, When the kill grace expires, Then the attempt ends at once with an ::error:: line naming the step instead of waiting for the step timeout
Given tests/ci/retry.sudo.test.ts fails or throws partway, When the test ends, Then any sudo sleep it started is killed (cleanup in finally)
Given the nested Vitest run in tests/ci/speed-limits.acceptance.test.ts exceeds its timeout, When it is stopped, Then the nested Vitest process and its children are killed, not only npx

Given retry.js times out an attempt whose command runs apt-get under sudo, When it stops the attempt, Then the root apt-get is really stopped (e.g. sudo -n kill on the process group) so it cannot keep holding the dpkg lock for the next attempt

implementationNotes:
AC added from TASK-1.29 follow-up (doc-27): the orphaned sudo'd apt-get (EPERM on kill) was the real cause of the CI lock failures.

2026-11-19: raised to High by the user after CI run #68 (main, 9ba77c8) failed: attempt 1's sudo apt-get (pid 5507) outlived its 240 s timeout and held the dpkg lock through attempts 2 and 3 (AC#4). Second CI failure from this cause.
